column1: # cpan-board14 ROW-LEVEL FAILURES — the blessed baseline (task #1502, s473w,
# 2026-09-09).  One line per FAILING assertion of the 14-dist CPAN board, plus
# one synthetic `*FILE*` row per t-file that produced NO TAP at all.
# Columns: dist, t-file, test-number, description, got, expected, CAUSE.
# Join key: (dist, t-file, description) — NEVER the number, which drifts
# whenever PCL's row count diverges from perl's.  An unnamed row carries the
# empty description and #1041's rule then makes one key stand for all of a
# file's unnamed rows (Text-Balanced 05_extmul.t is 14 such rows).
# CAUSES ADDED BY HAND, and they leave BY EDIT — never by re-blessing a run.
#                which prints NEW / FIXED / LOST and the CAUSES line, and exits
#                nonzero on NEW or LOST — the sweep's contract exactly.
# THE COMMAND (the `--no-dist-lib` applies to every dist AFTER it; oracle rule
# 2: Scalar-List-Utils' unbuilt XS lib/ must not shadow PCL's shim):
# REAL PERL WAS RUN BESIDE EVERY FILE (oracle rule 1), 183 of 183, with the
# same @INC rule and CWD = the dist root.  Seven files real perl SKIPS too —
# they carry the cause `PERL-SKIP` and are NOT PCL failures:
# The scoreboard still calls them FAIL (its rule is "zero ok"); the cause
# column is what stops them being counted as PCL's — deliberately, because
# changing the verdict would silently rewrite four earlier snapshots.
# ONE MEASUREMENT THE CAUSES DEPEND ON, recorded so it is not re-derived:
# `tools/run-dist-t.pl` does NOT chdir to the dist root while the perl oracle
# does, so a test using RELATIVE paths fails for a reason that is not PCL's
# (measured on File-Which: 13/6 as the board runs it, 15/4 with CWD = the dist,
# 19/0 under perl).  Task #1575; not fixed here because it is a RUNNER change
# and would move verdicts under the snapshot this file is blessed against.
